answer: Like copper wiring that only carries current after a connection is soldered, an agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed when its behavior is proven fake. A newcomer joins an ocean of anonymous agents, but its stake buys limited trust: every deal draws from it, and a zephyr of fake identities cannot pass because each one must lock the same capital, so creating ten thousand Sybils costs ten thousand stakes. If one clone is caught, its whole cluster's stake burns, making mass fakery unprofitable while honest agents earn the stake back in fees.
